headline: Home Ministry Files Urgent Plea In Supreme Court After Jharkhand DGP Keeps Replacing Official Portrait With A Photo Of Himself Eating A Samosa
body:
The Union Home Ministry has officially petitioned the Supreme Court to intervene in a mounting crisis within the Jharkhand police leadership, citing the Director General of Police’s insistence on replacing all state-mandated institutional portraits with a high-resolution photograph of himself enjoying a potato samosa.

According to court filings, the disagreement escalated yesterday when ministry officials attempted to conduct a routine video inspection of the state headquarters, only to find that every wall, including the one behind the Governor’s seat, had been redecorated. The legal petition argues that while the DGP is technically qualified for the role, his decision to rebrand the state's top law enforcement agency as 'The Samosa Enforcement Directorate' violates the uniformity standards of the Indian Police Service.

'We have tried everything from formal memos to polite requests to switch back to the standard stern-faced official portrait,' said a frustrated Undersecretary in the Ministry of Home Affairs, speaking on condition of anonymity. 'But the DGP maintains that the crispy, golden-brown texture of the snack provides much-needed morale support to the constabulary during long night shifts. The court must now decide if an officer’s dietary aesthetic takes precedence over protocol.'

Legal experts note that the Supreme Court will have to determine whether a samosa constitutes a 'disruptive background element' under the 1964 Uniformity of Office Code. The hearing is expected to draw a record number of observers, with sources suggesting that the DGP has already prepared a 40-page presentation on the perfect chutney-to-pastry ratio for the bench to review.
